concerns.text: Task T091 [P] [US2] is placed in Phase 2 and marked completed, but it depends on frequency‑distribution data that is only produced later in Phase 4 (tasks T018a, T018b, T019a/b). This consumer‑before‑producer ordering violates the foundational‑tasks‑first rule and makes the hard guard impossible to satisfy at execution time.

Task T015 (Compute anisotropy deviation) lists a dependency on T043, yet T043 (Bootstrap Convergence Check) is defined much later in Phase 5. This creates a consumer‑before‑producer dependency, breaking the required artifact flow.

Phase 2 mixes a user‑story‑specific task (T091, belonging to US2) with foundational infrastructure tasks. User‑story blocks must be independently shippable; mixing US2 tasks before the full data‑loader and frequency‑distribution pipeline (Phase 4) prevents US2 from being implemented in isolation.
T015 also references T043, which itself depends on T026 (null‑distribution generation) defined in Phase 5. This indirect forward dependency further compounds the ordering violation.

Tasks for German (DE) and Spanish (ES) language pipelines (e.g., token attribution, frequency distribution) are absent, while the specification (FR‑003, FR‑006, FR‑008) requires them. Although this is a coverage issue, the missing producer tasks cause downstream consumer tasks (e.g., T021, T022) to lack required inputs, leading to hidden ordering gaps.
